## Sparse history (C6) [`history_sweep.csv`, `history_smallest.csv`]
* Smallest setting within 10 % of full-history RMSE (point; CI-upper in the file): history fraction mteb_eng 0.25 (CI-upper 0.5), mteb_multi 0.5, helm_mmlu 1.0
  (none smaller); random missing cells down to density 0.5 on all three (helm_mmlu CI-upper 0.7); no tried density under the weak-model missingness pattern (down to 0.3).
* Not run on the union matrix (overlap too small, below).

## Small panels and the union matrix [`small_panels*.csv`, `union_overlap.csv`] (descriptive only, no k*, no H1/H2/H4 verdict)
* HELM Lite (10 scenarios), HELM Capabilities (5) and a 25-model x 16-benchmark union of HELM Lite and Open LLM Leaderboard (12 families) are case studies with N < 12;
  the name-matching rule and the exclusion of ambiguous names are in `union_overlap.py`. Overlaps: 25 models in HELM Lite and Open LLM Leaderboard, 23 with LiveBench,
  72 models in at least two sources; the complete-case union used is the 25 x 16 block above.

## Conditions to carry into the text
* Every statement is about standardised RMSE on held-out families; "closure" is relative to the LOBO reference, not to the noise floor.
* The in-sample optimistic reference and the oracle selector are test-leaking and appear only as labelled bounds.
* MTEB matrices are dense pools chosen by us (see `datasets.csv`); HELM MMLU has a binomial sampling floor [`helm_mmlu_binomial_floor.csv`].
# Results and the conditions they hold under (experiment-repo, as of commit after 077ae91)

Every number below is read from a file in `results/` (file named in brackets). Primary design: grouped 10-fold by model family (21 / 247-column MTEB multi / 79 HELM
models), fixed 30 % target columns, greedy A-optimal selector, FA predictor unless said otherwise; intervals are family-clustered bootstrap (B=2000, seed 0).
Metrics are RMSE on the original standardised scale. Transform (identity or logit) was chosen on training folds by held-out likelihood:
helm_mmlu logit, mteb_eng identity, mteb_multi logit [`transform.csv`]. Departures from the Brief are in `code/DEVIATIONS.md`.

## H2: greedy A vs random, grid average over k=1..min(10,N/2) [`gap.csv`, `robustness.csv`]
* Gap in RMSE (greedy A minus random), CI: helm_mmlu -0.044 [-0.065, -0.026] (-7.6 % of random); mteb_eng -0.038 [-0.058, -0.013] (-6.1 %);
  mteb_multi -0.076 [-0.085, -0.066] (-11.3 %). The CI excludes 0 on all three; the pre-registered margin (gap >= 10 % of random RMSE) is met only on mteb_mult

cat > /tmp/c6.md <<'E'
M1 is delivered: the grouped protocol now runs on the real sparse MTEB matrix. Code and results are in experiment-repo `main` (c2d1f24 plus a wording fix) and in paper-repo `dev` (4aaa293). The full account is in the "Sparse leaderboard matrix" section of `code/RESULTS.md`, with the departures in `code/DEVIATIONS.md` item 14.

**Conditions**
- **Data:** MTEB score matrices with their real missing cells (NaN), 6 subsets from 21 % to 70 % observed. `sparse_subsets.csv` lists models x tasks, density, median observed cells per model, tested models, families and organisations.
  - `eng_full`: English tasks seen by at least 20 models, 445 x 335, 21 % observed, median 60 cells per model, 337 models tested.
  - `eng_d30`, `eng_d50`, `eng_d70`: English subsets trimmed to 30, 50 and 70 % observed. Sizes are 332x295, 268x176 and 226x134, with 215-332 models tested.
  - `all_d30`, `all_d50`: all tasks, trimmed to 30 and 50 %. Sizes are 331x705 and 236x517, with median 181 and 308 cells per model.
- **Split and test models:** grouped 10-fold, held out by model family. A model is tested if it has at least 30 observed cells. Training columns need at least 10 observed training cells and are standardised on their observed cells. Identity transform only.
- **Candidates and targets:** for each tested model and each of 3 partitions, the targets T are a random 30 % of its observed cells and the candidates C are the rest of its observed cells.
- **Selectors:** greedy A runs on the masked-EM factor-model covariance. Random uses 30 draws per k.
- **Predictors:**
  - `colmean`.
  - `fa`: masked-EM factor model, rank chosen by inner 5-fold masked marginal likelihood with the one-SE rule.
  - `pw`: pairwise-complete correlation, PSD-clipped and shrunk toward the identity.
  - `softimpute`: masked Soft-Impute fold-in.
  - `fa` and `pw` are the two best predictors that handle missing cells.
- **LOBO analogue:** all of C predicts T, using `fa` and `pw`; the reference is the lower of the two (`lobo` rows in `sparse_refs.csv`). Closure is therefore not capped at 1.
- **Grid:** k = 1..6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20. There is no k=30, because C holds at most 70 % of a model's 30-100 observed cells.
- **Intervals:** family-clustered bootstrap, B=2000, seed 0. A k* that is never reached on the grid is censored.

**Results** (CIs are in the CSVs)
- Greedy A beats random at every k on every subset, for both `fa` and `pw`. The gap CI excludes 0 in every cell except `pw` at k=20 on `eng_full`, where it is [-0.105, 0.005].
- At k=3 with `fa`, the relative gap to random is 6-7 % on the English subsets, 14 % on `all_d30` and 24 % on `all_d50`.
- Closure at k=3, greedy A (`fa` / `pw`):

| Subset | `fa` | `pw` |
|---|---|---|
| `eng_full` | 0.76 | 0.79 |
| `eng_d30` | 0.79 | 0.79 |
| `eng_d50` | 0.78 | 0.78 |
| `eng_d70` | 0.80 | 0.80 |
| `all_d30` | 0.75 | 0.78 |
| `all_d50` | 0.72 | 0.71 |

- Random selection at k=3 with `pw` reaches closure 0.55-0.74.
- k*(0.9) with greedy A and `pw` is 6, 8, 12, 8, 10 and 20 for `eng_full`, `eng_d30`, `eng_d50`, `eng_d70`, `all_d30` and `all_d50`.
- Random with `fa` never reaches 0.9 on the grid on any subset. Random with `pw` is 20 on `eng_full` and `eng_d50`, 15 on `eng_d70`, and censored on the others.
- The k* intervals are wide, for example [3, >20] on `eng_full`. Do not report a k* value without its interval.
- `fa` is best or tied at k up to 5, and `pw` is slightly better at k=8 or more. Both are far better than `colmean`. `softimpute` is only slightly better than `colmean`, because its fold-in shrinks cells it cannot see.
- **Claim for the main text:** greedy A beats random on the sparse matrix at every density from 21 % to 70 %, with closure about 0.7-0.8 at k=3. The two supporting results are the gap CI at k=3 and closure at k=3 with greedy A against random under `pw`. k*(0.9) is secondary because of the intervals.

shown.message:
I've run the grouped protocol on the real sparse MTEB matrix and closed experiment-repo#6. The six full runs finished and the results are in experiment-repo `main` and paper-repo `dev` (4aaa293).

**What was run:**
- Six subsets with real missing cells, from 21 % to 70 % observed. `eng_full` is the English tasks seen by at least 20 models (21 %). The 30, 50 and 70 % subsets are trimmed English pools, plus two all-task pools at 30 and 50 %.
- Each tested model has at least 30 observed cells. Targets are a random 30 % of its observed cells and candidates are the rest.
- Greedy A is compared with random and the column mean. Three predictors handle missing cells: the masked-EM factor model, pairwise-complete correlation and Soft-Impute.
- The leave-one-benchmark-out analogue predicts the targets from all candidates. Intervals are family-clustered bootstrap.

**What it shows:**
- **Greedy A vs random:** greedy A beats random at every k on every subset for the factor model and pairwise predictors. The one exception is the pairwise predictor at k=20 on `eng_full`, where the interval is [-0.105, 0.005].
- **Size of the gap at k=3:** the factor-model gap is 6–7 % of random on the English subsets, 14 % on `all_d30` and 24 % on `all_d50`.
- **Closure at k=3:** greedy A reaches closure 0.71–0.80 at k=3, against 0.55–0.74 for random with the pairwise predictor.
- **k\* at closure 0.9:** greedy A with the pairwise predictor reaches it at k=6–12 on the English subsets and `all_d30`, and at k=20 on `all_d50`. Its intervals are wide, so I flagged it as secondary.
- **Soft-Impute:** it is only slightly better than the column mean.

**Caveats:**
- The grid stops at k=20, because a tested model has only 30–100 observed cells and the candidates are 70 % of them. There is no k=30.
- Identity transform only; nothing below 21 % observed.
- RMSE levels are not comparable with the dense pools.
- Because the reference is the lower of two predictors, closure can exceed 1.
- Runs use 3 partitions × 30 draws, where the dense runs use 50.

I opened issues in `figtab-repo` (#5) and `paper-repo` (#8) pointing at the CSVs, the conditions and which result carries the claim.
